text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered for private-gpu-cluster-nyc — capacity_exhaustion (P1) :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Symptoms: queued requests spike, autoscaler failed to allocate new GPU nodes, 503s observed for customer acme-health.
jamie: oncall here, seeing queue growth to ~4.2k reqs and 95% GPU utilization on pool-a. tagging infra. @anika @morgan
anika: joining — can you paste the autoscaler logs? are there imagepullbackoff traces or rate-limit errors?
morgan: looks like the autoscaler is hitting scale_limits: "max_nodes_per_cluster" enforced by customer's config. cluster shows 0/4 pending node creates due to quota check failing in our control plane.
taylor: I see node-provision requests being NACKed by the provider: "quotaExceeded: VPC NIC quota" in the agent logs. also a bunch of warmup timeouts: node bootstrap took >15m.
jamie: customer has reserved pool set to 16 gpus, current desired 16 and max 16. autoscaler is trying to spin new nodes but blocked. we need a mitigation path.
lina: customer CS here (acme-health) — customers on two endpoints report degraded inferencing, some timeouts. no reported data exfiltration, but SLAs affected. current impact: ~25% of requests returning 503s, others high latency.
raj: quick assessment: can we failover critical traffic to hosted fallback pool for their org? that reduces latency but incurs cost and potential data routing constraints.
chen: running the runbook step to free up reserved pool slots: `/runbook private-cluster node-eviction-safe` — note this will evict low-priority workloads first. anyone object?
morgan: okay to evict ephemeral batch jobs, but don't evict pinned customer workloads. which namespaces are safe?
jamie: namespace tag: infra-batch, ci-warmup, ai-bench are safe. run eviction with `--grace-period 60` and monitor.
runbook-bot: Confirmed: Eviction policy applied to namespaces [infra-batch, ci-warmup, ai-bench]. Starting prioritized pod eviction.
taylor: triggered pod evictions, saw immediate drop in GPU allocation, but autoscaler still queues node creates; provider still NACKing because VPC NIC quota.
anika: can we request temporary NIC quota bump for the customer's VPC? that's a manual ticket to the provider, may take 30-60m. not ideal for immediate mitigation.
jamie: immediate plan: 1) failover critical routes to hosted fallback for acme-health (duration: minutes), 2) continue evict noncritical pods, 3) open provider quota ticket, 4) prepare rollback. who will own each?
raj: I can initiate hosted fallback routes and inform the customer. doing DNS edge routing toggle now, will confirm once CNAME changes propagate.
lina: please include customer in comms: sending note to their SRE and saying we're failing over to hosted to restore throughput, ETA ~5-10m.
runbook-bot: Command executed: `toggle-hosted-fallback --org acme-health --routes inference-primary,inference-secondary` — waiting for confirmation.
raj: hosted failover confirmed for inference-primary — traffic at ~60% now flowing to hosted instances, 503s drop to ~6%. still monitoring.
chen: while failover is live, we should try to reduce node warmup time: cache AMI pull, pre-warm init container, and ensure kubelet certs ready. triggering a warmup job to pre-pull images to the node template.
morgan: submitted warmup job to edge image cache; should reduce bootstrap from ~15m to ~2-3m. once provider quota is resolved, autoscaler should succeed faster.
anika: provider ticket ID 123456 opened for NIC quota. ETA quoted 48m but escalation requested.
jamie: customer impact update: now 98% of traffic served, a small portion still hitting degraded path. Lina pls confirm comms.
lina: informed customer SRE and sent status update: fallback enabled, eviction completed, provider ticket opened. Customer acknowledged and thanks team for quick mitigation.
taylor: action items: follow up with provider until quota increase done; monitor node creates and remove fallback once cluster normal.
jamie: handing off to next oncall, @chen you have the lead for the follow-up window. I'll update the incident board and close pager when provider confirms quota and autoscaler returns to normal.
chen: taking over. will keep watch for 2 hours and coordinate with provider + customer. adding timeline and notes to incident doc: https://redwood/internal/incidents/2890012345
jamie: thanks team — great coordination. :thumbsup:
